title: LitCalMissalWritePayload
description: Single sanctorale ENTRY write payload for PUT/PATCH /missals/{missal_id}/{event_key}. The entry is identified by the URL, never by the body: `event_key` may be repeated here, but only with the value already in the path — a mismatch is refused rather than applied, because renaming a key would orphan its i18n and lectionary sidecar entries permanently. Every structure property is optional at the schema level so PATCH can be genuinely partial; the API handler (MissalsHandler) requires the full set on PUT and at least one changed field on PATCH. The `i18n` and `readings` sidecars accept only locales the target folder already carries a file for — adding a locale to a Missal changes the locale set the /missals index advertises and is a separate act, so the handler refuses an unknown one rather than creating the file.

Locale.title: Locale
Locale.description: A locale as the sanctorale source tree spells it in a file name: a two- or three-letter language, optionally with a region (`la`, `en_US`, `it_IT`). The handler additionally requires that a file for this locale already exists in the target folder, so no path is ever derived from an unvalidated string.

I18n.title: I18n
I18n.description: The event's name per locale. An empty string is meaningful and allowed: it is how the corpus records `this key exists but has not been translated yet`, which is what keeps every locale file a complete, diffable inventory of what still needs translating.

Readings.title: Readings
Readings.description: The event's lectionary readings per locale. Written to the Missal's own lectionary folder when it has one (the national editions), or to the rite-level sanctorum corpus when the Missal has none but the rite does (the editiones typicae) — the same tiers GET /lectionary/{rite}/sanctorale reports. A rite with no lectionary corpus of its own and no rite-wide corpus to fall back to (the Ambrosian rite today, see #957) has nowhere to write readings, so the handler REJECTS a payload carrying this property for such a Missal; omit `readings` entirely.
